prompt: A roof truss is the isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $\overline{AB} \cong \overline{AC}$, so $B$ and $C$ are the base corners. The rafter is extended past $B$, forming an exterior angle at $B$ of $125^\circ$. Find the measure, in degrees, of the vertex angle $\angle A$.
hint: The exterior angle at $B$ and the interior angle $\angle B$ form a linear pair.

hints.text: The exterior angle at $B$ and the interior angle $\angle B$ form a linear pair.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with a friendlier exterior angle: if it were $130^\circ$, then $\angle B = 50^\circ$, $\angle C = 50^\circ$, and $\angle A = 180 - 100 = 80^\circ$. Run those same three steps on $125$.
$\angle B = 180 - 125 = 55^\circ$, and $\angle C$ equals $\angle B$ because the truss is isosceles.

explanation: The exterior angle at $B$ and the interior $\angle B$ sit along a straight rafter: $\angle B = 180 - 125 = 55^\circ$.
Because $\overline{AB} \cong \overline{AC}$, the base angles are congruent, so $\angle C = 55^\circ$ too.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the Exterior Angle Theorem instead
steps: The exterior angle at $B$ equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, $\angle A + \angle C$, so $\angle A + \angle C = 125^\circ$.
Since $\angle C = 55^\circ$ from the linear pair and the isosceles property, $\angle A = 125 - 55 = 70^\circ$. Same answer, different route.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is using $125^\circ$ as if it were an interior angle of the truss — that immediately blows the $180^\circ$ budget once you add two base angles.

An exterior angle is always OUTSIDE the triangle. Convert it first with a linear pair ($180 - 125 = 55$), and only then do triangle work. The second trap is stopping at 55, which is a base angle, not the vertex angle asked for.
